reason_registered: The initial 64-query workload had zero warm misses with both default and 256-entry caches. Retain that result; add an explicitly separate 768-query working set to measure capacity pressure instead of attributing its speedup to cache size.
hypothesis: The 0.11.0 default cache should reduce misses and warm latency when the working set exceeds 0.10.0's default. Equal small caches should remove most capacity-driven gains. Report actual occupancy and misses even if this hypothesis fails.
timing: Same persistent-worker RPC scope and continuation checks as the initial plan; no lexical matches, one explicit required document per query, 768 distinct queries.
statistics: Eight paired process sessions per mode, alternating version order, 2000 fixed-seed bootstrap draws of session medians.
improvement_threshold: At least 10% paired median latency reduction with descriptive 95% interval above zero. Cache-capacity claim additionally requires fewer default-cache misses and no comparable benefit with equal small caches.
resource_watch: Report peak RSS and bounded cache occupancy; flag median RSS increase over 20%.
